title: Give the agent fleet a non-elevated restart path for trading-server (kill the SYSTEM-admin dependency on redeploys)
description:
## Problem

Every time `dist` is rebuilt, the running `trading-server` on `localhost:4242` must be restarted to adopt the new build. Today that restart needs **Administrator / LOCAL_SYSTEM on PG-DEVOPS14**, because the PM2 daemon + `trading-server` are launched at boot by the `PM2 Resurrect` scheduled task running as **LOCAL_SYSTEM / highest** (`ops/install-pm2-autostart.ps1`, TRA-605). The agent fleet runs as the non-elevated user `PRIMEROGA\eetienne`, so:

- `pm2 restart trading-server` -> EPERM on the SYSTEM daemon control pipe
- `taskkill /F` on the worker -> Access denied
- triggering the `PM2 Resurrect` task -> Access denied (and `pm2 resurrect` does not restart an already-running app)
- no HTTP self-restart route exists

This is why [TRA-792](/TRA/issues/TRA-792) is blocked on a human/operator restart. It will recur on every future redeploy.

## Options (pick one)

- **B1 (recommended, smallest):** add an authenticated `POST /api/admin/restart` (requireAuth + requireAdmin) that flushes state and calls `process.exit(0)`. Under PM2 `autorestart: true` the daemon relaunches the worker onto the current `dist`. Fully agent-serviceable with the existing admin token. Guard it well

title: Fix mobile scroll on public landing page (TRA-754)
description:
## Fix: public landing page can't scroll on mobile (board-reported)

Reported by the board on the umbrella [TRA-754](/TRA/issues/TRA-754): the **front/landing page is broken on the mobile app — it can't scroll**, so everything below the hero (value pillars, strategy strip, how-it-works, secondary CTA, and the required **risk disclaimer**) is unreachable. The risk disclosure being scroll-locked off-screen is a compliance issue, not just cosmetics — this is **high priority**.

### Root cause (diagnosed)
`apps/desktop/src/index.css`:
- `.lp` (line ~3310) uses `min-height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh; overflow-y: auto;`
- Its parent `body` (line ~153) is `height: 100vh; height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden;` (the app-shell pattern, used by `.app` too).

`min-height` does **not bound** the box, so `.lp` grows to its full content height and `overflow-y: auto` never produces a scroll region. The fixed, `overflow:hidden` body then clips everything past the first viewport. On a tall desktop window more content fits above the fold, so the break is most visible on narrow/short (mobile) viewports. Live equity **short** (sell-to-open) OTOCO brackets are being submitted on the production Tradier account and **rejected**, because the account appears to be a **cash account** (Tradier "Settled Funds" / "Available Funds" terminology) and cash accounts cannot sell short.

## Evidence (board incident 2026-06-08, [TRA-335](/TRA/issues/TRA-335))

The ORB / BB-fade / Ichimoku strategies legitimately emit short signals, and `placeTradierEquityBracket` passes `side: signal.side` straight through to `submitBracketOrder`, so shorts are sent unconditionally.

[TRA-711](/TRA/issues/TRA-711) gates the 1-share floor + caps size on **available funds**, which incidentally suppressed *all* opens (long and short) while Available Funds was $0.06. Once the account is funded, `sizeLiveEquityFromStop` (which is side-agnostic) will size a short > 0 and submit it again -> guaranteed reject on a cash account. So this resurfaces the moment buying power returns.

title: Durable live-equity arming — boot a live engine from persisted settings so liveEquityClientConfigured survives restarts
description:
## Problem

TRA-580 acceptance (capture the first organic live equity OTOCO fill) keeps getting blocked because the live-equity arm does NOT survive a server restart. Every restart drops it:

- 16:00Z restart (build 6cdf66c): `liveEngineCount` 1->0, `liveEquityClientConfigured` true->false.
- Board accepted re-arm confirmation `1152c9f4` on TRA-712; a 16:49Z restart (build cfd9427) again booted un-armed. `/api/health/live-equity` -> `liveEngineCount:0`, `liveEquityClientConfigured:false`, `productionEngineCount:1`, `liveEquityTradingEnabled:true`.

So the monitor can never catch a fill: a one-time board re-arm is wiped by the next restart.

## Root cause (traced)

At boot, `initAllUserContexts()` builds each engine from persisted on-disk settings: `new SignalEngine(settings, tracker, sharedRvScanner)` (user-context.ts:688). The live-equity client is built in the constructor only when `settings.mode === 'live'` (signal-engine.ts:719-723 -> `buildTradierLiveEquityClient`, defined at signal-engine.ts:4358). `buildTradierLiveEquityClient` ALREADY has a production env-fallback for creds (`TRADIER_API_TOKEN` / `TRADIER_ACCOUNT_ID`, signal-engine.ts:4364-4376) - so creds are NOT the gap.

title: P0-2a: Implement Live-Trading Promotion Gate enforcement in app
description:
Implement the **Live-Trading Promotion Gate** in the trading app so no strategy can flip to LIVE unless it has passed the backtest + paper-trade criteria. Quant criteria are defined in the [TRA-527](/TRA/issues/TRA-527) gate-spec document: /TRA/issues/TRA-527#document-gate-spec

## What to build
1. **Per-strategy `promotion_status`** with stage state:
   - `backtest`: pass | fail | missing
   - `paper`: pass | fail | missing (+ paper trade count)
   - `signoff`: present | absent
2. **Gate the mode switch / "go live" control**: refuse enabling live unless `backtest=pass AND paper=pass AND signoff=present`. A blocked attempt must surface which gate failed.
3. **Compute metrics from data, not hand-entry** — Sharpe, expectancy, profit factor, max drawdown, trade counts, realized-vs-modeled slippage are derived by the app from (a) the backtest run output and (b) the paper-trade ledger. This prevents gaming the gate by typing numbers.
4. **Thresholds in config** (v1 defaults in the spec): Sharpe>=1.0 / expectancy>0 / profit factor>=1.3 / maxDD<=20% / >=100 backtest trades for Stage 1; >=50 paper trades, paper expectancy>0 and >=0.5x backtest expectancy, paper Sharpe>=0.8, slippage<=1.5x

title: Annualize paper Sharpe in promotion gate to match backtest scale (TRA-532 verify fix)
description:
QuantTrader verification of the Live-Trading Promotion Gate ([TRA-532](/TRA/issues/TRA-532), commit `c4ee5aa`) found **one criteria defect**: the Stage-2 paper Sharpe is on a different scale than the Stage-1 backtest Sharpe, so the `≥0.8` bar does not mean what the [TRA-527](/TRA/issues/TRA-527#document-gate-spec) spec intends. This issue tracks the fix. Everything else in the gate was verified correct.

## The defect
- **Stage-1 backtest Sharpe** (`packages/backtest/src/portfolio-runner.ts`) is **annualized**: `meanRet/stdRet × √barsPerYear` over the bar-return series — a standard Sharpe. The per-trade form is only a fallback when there is ≤1 bar return.
- **Stage-2 paper Sharpe** (`packages/shared/src/promotion-gate.ts` → `computePaperGateMetrics`) is a **per-trade information ratio** `mean(R)/stdev(R)`, **un-annualized**, judged against `≥0.8`.

These are incomparable scales. A per-trade IR of 0.8 is ~4–10× what real strategies produce (typical per-trade IR ≈ 0.05–0.20). As written, Stage 2 rejects essentially every genuine strategy regardless of true quality — fail-closed for the wrong reason — and pressures operators into loosen-overrides, defeating the gate. The spec's 0.8 is

Observed in `/api/state` `account.openPositions` during the [TRA-518](/TRA/issues/TRA-518) post-market review (Tue 2026-06-02, demo mode):

Risk-management exits silently don't engage on affected positions. In live mode this would let a loser run past its intended stop.

- Add a guard/test so positions can't be opened with a stop/target on the wrong side of entry.

title: Phase 3 broker reconciliation & data-feed hardening (TRA-402 §5)
description:
Spun out of [TRA-402](/TRA/issues/TRA-402) review (see `review-report` document, §5).

## Scope (checklist)
- **Reconcile on boot.** Perp reconciliation runs every 5 min but not at startup — a position opened on the Coinbase UI is invisible for up to 5 min, risking a duplicate. Run reconcile once on boot before the first trading tick.
- **Equity reconciliation.** Tradier equity positions have no periodic reconcile; add one (options already has it).
- **Partial-fill handling.** Options close/exit reconciliation does not handle partial fills end-to-end; parse `avg_fill_price`/`fill_quantity`, close the filled qty, re-order the remainder.
- **Per-user rate-limit breaker.** The Tradier 429 circuit breaker is per-process — one user's rate-limit blocks all users. Scope it per-user/token.
- **Data-feed freshness gating.** Candle/quote caches are used even when stale; add a quote-age check before running strategies and ordered failover across feeds.

## Acceptance
- A position opened out-of-band is detected on next boot, not after 5 min.
- Partial fills produce correct position + P&L state.
- One user's rate-limit no longer blocks others.

title: Crypto dashboard shows no prices for demo users — restore resilient quote source
description:
## P1 — from TRA-436 regression test

On production (`tradingai-bqb1.onrender.com`) every one of the 50 crypto symbols on the Crypto dashboard renders **"Quote unavailable — provider rate-limited"**. Demo crypto users have **no working quote source**.

### Root cause
In `packages/server/src/crypto-engine.ts` `doTick()` calls `fetchCryptoQuotes(activeSymbols)`. title: Auto-reprice pending Tradier sell-to-close orders (fill-chaser) so closes don't stall
description:
## Problem

During a live Tradier session, the trade engine (TradeAI) trailed and tried to close out option positions, but **most `sell_to_close` orders got stuck `pending`**. The operator had to manually cancel each pending sell and re-submit at a lower limit (~$1 lower — e.g. mid 17 stuck pending → 16 fills) to get filled.

Reported on [TRA-390](/TRA/issues/TRA-390).

## Root cause (engine behavior today)

`submitSmartSellToClose` in `packages/server/src/tradier-smart-close.ts` walks the limit price **mid → bid+25%-of-spread** over only `maxAttempts` (default 2) attempts with a ~5s wait each, then returns `status: 'pending'` and **leaves the last limit order live on Tradier**.

The per-tick reconciler `reconcilePendingCloseOrder` then only **polls order status** — it never re-prices. So a pending close sits at the original limit indefinitely until the operator manually cancels and reprices down. That is exactly the manual workaround the operator described.

## Requested change — auto-reprice (fill-chaser) for pending close orders

Extend the close path so a `pending` `sell_to_close` is automatically walked down toward the bid until it fills, instead of stalling.

Without this fix, every future strategy evaluation will:
- pass on majors and fail on small-caps for the wrong reason (cost model, not strategy);
- force ad-hoc universe restrictions on each strategy ticket.

title: Cost-aware retest filter: skip signals where cost burden dominates R:R
description:
## Goal

Restore the retest entry path to **avgRR >= 0** by skipping signals where the cost burden mathematically dominates per-trade R:R.

## Why

[TRA-181](/TRA/issues/TRA-181) ran a five-axis knob sweep on 365d × 1h × 6 crypto symbols and found avgRR clusters near **-3.0R** for every N>=30 config. The dominant factor is cost arithmetic, not entry timing:

- 40 bps × 2 (round-trip commission) + 10 bps slippage ≈ **0.9% of notional**
- Hourly crypto retest stops average ~0.5% of price
- Cost / risk ≈ 1.8R per trade → even a stop-out registers as ~-2.8R

The retest entry tightens stops (good for theoretical R:R) but proportionally worsens the cost-to-risk ratio. The volume-gate axis (`retestRequireVolumeIncrease=true`) hinted at the path forward — N=5 / win 60% / +0.12% return on 365d — but its filter is too coarse to clear N>=30.

## Investigation

Add a **cost-aware retest filter**: at the moment a retest fires, compute the expected round-trip cost as a fraction of the proposed stop distance, and skip the entry when the ratio exceeds a configurable floor. Two candidate knobs to expose on `ReversalOptions` / `BacktestReversalOpts`:

- `retestMinStopPct?: number` — minimum retest s

title: RiskManager: cap position notional at fraction of equity (no-cap bug surfaced by TRA-168 round 2)
description:
## Critical: position size has no notional cap

`packages/engine/src/risk.ts:68-72` (`RiskManager.sizeFromStop`) divides the per-trade risk budget by the stop distance and floors to whole shares. There is **no cap on resulting notional**.

When a strategy uses an ATR-derived or BB-derived stop that's small relative to entry price, position size becomes enormous. Round-2 backtest evidence (cost-aware Yahoo 90 d × 1 h × BTC):

```
MACD-BB (stock params)   trades=13   return=-30,981%
MACD-BB (crypto tuned)   trades=7    return=-30,959%
```

That is not a strategy failure — it is a 60×+ leverage event. With a tiny stop distance (e.g. 0.05% of price) the risk-budget math sizes to ~60 BTC at $60k = $3.6M notional on a $100k account. Round-trip commission alone (40 bps × 2 = 80 bps × $3.6M = $28,800) far exceeds the supposed $500 risk budget.

In live trading the broker rejects orders past buying power, but **the engine itself enforces nothing**, which means:

1. Backtests are mathematically unbounded and produce nonsense numbers (-30,000%).
2. Live trading silently relies on broker buying-power limits as the only safety net.
3. A bug in margin reporting or a partial-fill scenario could p

title: Backtest framework: commissions, slippage, fill realism, and missing strategies
description:
Backtest framework currently produces unreliable results because:

1. **Zero commission/slippage modeling** — Coinbase 0.4% taker fees alone wipe most edges. Backtest assumes free perfect fills.

5. **No equity historical backtest** — only crypto via Yahoo 1h (`backtest-crypto.ts`). No equivalent script for SPY/QQQ/AAPL.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add `commissionBps` and `slippageBps` to `BacktestConfig`. Deduct on every fill (entry + exit). Default to 40 bps (Coinbase taker) for crypto, 5 bps (slippage only) for equities.

title: Security: default admin account seeded with weak password (1234)
description:
In packages/server/src/users.ts:57, when no users.json exists (fresh install or after reset), the server seeds a default admin account with username "admin" and password "1234". For a live trading app this is a critical security risk if the password is not immediately changed.

**Fix:** Require the admin password to be set via an environment variable (e.g. DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD) on first boot, or remove the seed entirely and require an explicit setup step. Reject startup if the env var is not set in production mode.

title: TRA-56: P0 Bug Fixes — Correct exit price and remove ORB from crypto
description: ## Context UX review ([TRA-56](/TRA/issues/TRA-56)) found two P0 bugs in `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`. ## Fix 1: Closed-position exit price is wrong **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` (both Stocks and Crypto Positions tab) **Problem:** The exit price for closed positions is computed as: ```tsx p.side === 'buy' ? p.takeProfit : p.stopLoss ``` This always shows the *planned* exit price regardless of how the trade actually closed. A buy trade that hit its stop-loss will incorrectly display the take-profit price, producing a wrong P&L figure. **Fix:** 1. Check if `Position` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` has an `exitPrice` field. If not, add `exitPrice?: number` to the interface. 2. title: validation-progress harness charges the spread TWICE: netPnl = (fill-to-fill) − fees − |fill−mid| (paper-accrual-validation.ts:188-203)
description:
Parent: TRA-4728. Found while decomposing the OTM sleeve's −$18.86/trade (`/api/health/validation-progress`, live `c94a5deb`, 2026-09-19T19:07Z).

## Defect
`pairFillsIntoRoundTrips` (`packages/server/src/paper-accrual-validation.ts:188-203`, same bytes on `c94a5deb` and `origin/main`):

```
grossPnl = (closePrice − openPrice) × 100 × matched   // FILL prices: already include the spread paid
slippageCost = |openPrice − openMid| + |closePrice − closeMid|  (×100×matched)
netPnl = grossPnl − fees − slippageCost            // spread subtracted a SECOND time
```

`grossPnl` is built from the executed fill prices, so the crossing cost is already inside it. Subtracting `slippageCost` again counts it twice. The `abs()` also turns price improvement into a cost: RIG's exit filled at 0.18 against a 0.16 mid, and that is charged as −$2.

## Measured impact (the 6 live `single_leg_otm` round-trips, rebuilt to the cent from `/api/health/live-options-fee-slippage` `records[]`)
| | served | correct (cash) |

title: The per-cell tape-expectancy row carries no provenance — a cost-bar admit reads identically whether the cell is desk real-money or mid-booked demo tape
description:
Residual of TRA-4569. **Instrument hardening only — this changes no gate verdict and blocks nothing.**

## The defect

`arm.costBar.edge.otmCells[]` (`/api/health/live-enforce-gates`) and `table.cells[]`
(`/api/health/option-expectancy-table`) publish `n / meanR_gate / sdR_gate / seR_gate / lowerCI95 / barR / admits`
and **no per-cell provenance**. Provenance exists only at *table* level (`basis.desk` / `basis.unattributed` /
`basis.fixtureExcluded` / `basis.byMode`), which cannot be attributed down to the cell that decided a candidate.

This term is not decorative: `lowerCI95` **is** the edge side of the live `single_leg_otm` cost-bar admission
(`admit ⟺ mean(R_gate) − 1.96·SE ≥ admissionBarR`, TRA-3391). So a cell whose `admits` flips is a cell that opens
real-money positions.

**A cell reading `lowerCI95: 0.3617` is byte-identical whether it is 110 desk real-money closes or 84 July demo
rows booked at mid.** That is the failure mode: the instrument reads the same in the state where it is trustworthy
and the state where it is not.

Do NOT implement day trading, scalping, 0DTE trading, intraday momentum trading, or rapid options strategies at this stage.

Target holding period: approximately 3–20 trading days.

Find liquid OTM call and put options where:

4. The trade has positive expected value after spread, slippage and fees.
5. Risk is strictly defined.

The system should prioritize QUALITY over number of trades.

Preferred DTE:

* 21–60 DTE

* Puts: -0.25 to -0.40

* 0DTE

* Extremely far OTM options
* Illiquid contracts
* Wide bid/ask spreads

Look for:

description:

title: TRA-3368 residual: z=2.0 gives ~50% power at delta, not 80% -- pre-register the operating point (or document it)
description:
Split out of **TRA-3608** (the bqb1 deploy clearance for `2f24acc`, which I CLEARED — this is a strictly-later tightening, not a defect in it).

## The gap

`gate-power.ts` ships `POWER_CONFIDENCE_SIGMA = 2.0`, so `n_req = ceil((2*sigma/delta)^2)` puts delta at **two standard errors**. That is ~95% confidence against a **zero** effect, but only **~50% power at delta itself** — at a true effect of exactly delta, the estimate lands below the 2-SE line half the time.

So the word `powered: true` on `/api/health/live-capital-gate` does **not** mean "80% powered". A reader who takes it that way is over-reading the route by roughly a factor of two in sample.

## What the change would be

`z = 1.96 + 0.84 ~= 2.81` for true 80% power at delta. That multiplies every `n_req` by `(2.81/2)^2 ~= 1.97x`:

| c | n_req @ z=2.0 (shipped) | n_req @ z=2.81 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.03 | 138 | ~272 |
| 0.20 | 1112 | ~2195 |
| 0.30 | 1905 | ~3760 |

(Left column re-derived this run by running the shipped `sigmaParametric`/`requiredN`; right column is the 1.97x scaling and must be **re-measured with the shipped fn**, not taken from this table, before anything is written.)

title: Invert the desk fold from a reactive denylist to a KNOWN_DESK_BOOKS allowlist (CTO item C) — GATED on unrecognisedDeskBookCount accrual
description:
**Filed per CTO item C on TRA-2547: "yes, and you were right not to ride it along — own issue, own sign-off."**

## The class

`BUILTIN_TEST_PATTERNS` is a **reactive denylist**, and a reactive denylist has **no failing state**:
an unseen book name is **in** the board-facing number by default. Nothing goes red; the number is just
quietly wrong until a human happens to read the roster. That is why this class has now recurred four
times:

**TRA-1475 → TRA-1949 → TRA-2488 → TRA-2524.**

TRA-2524 added `/^tra\d/i`, `/^(ceo|cto|cfo|qt|leaddev)\d/i`, `/^qtprobe/i`. Those fix today's three
books. They do nothing about the next book that names itself after what it is verifying — which is
exactly how all three of the current ones got in.

Yes. If you're building this into your **options swing-trading app**, I would go beyond OTM mispricing and build a **library of independent signals**. The goal shouldn't be to find one strategy with a huge win rate—it should be to find several strategies whose edges work in different market regimes.

description:
**Filed off TRA-4424 (live-tape grade, 2026-09-10).** Source-verified; magnitude **unmeasured**.

`initAllUserContexts` (`user-context.ts:1403`) builds **one `SignalEngine` per user**. The sweep cursor
store (`tick-sweep-budget.ts` → `sweepCursors`) is **process-wide**, and `runBudgetedSweep`'s own

|---|---|

| `${this.mode}:cold-bar-scan` | ~14524 |

| `${this.mode}:social-curated` | ~21781 |
| `${this.mode}:mtf-refresh` | ~21892 |

symbols, open-option underlyings). A cursor symbol found in the other book's array resumes mid-list —
